main_result: The fabricated vertically coupled microrings achieve intrinsic Q factors of 4.0×10^5 in multimode devices and 3.4×10^5 in single-mode devices.
application_angle: The process could simplify scalable fabrication of resonators for electro-optic, nonlinear, filtering, and quantum-photonic circuits.

title: Probing injection locking of an integrated nanolaser pair through RF beating
abstract: We demonstrate simultaneous optical injection locking of an integrated pair of photonic-crystal nanolasers coupled to a common silicon waveguide. Due to fabrication-induced disorder, the two nanolasers exhibit distinct emission wavelengths, allowing their individual locking ranges to be resolved as a function of the injection-laser detuning and power. We identify a region where both nanolasers are simultaneously locked to the master laser. To probe this collective locked state, the two nanolasers are independently pump-modulated at distinct radio frequencies. A beat note at the difference frequency appears only within the overlap region, providing a direct RF signature of simultaneous locking. These results establish RF beating as a compact diagnostic of common-master injection locking in integrated nanolaser systems.
one_liner: Difference-frequency RF beating directly identifies simultaneous injection locking of two integrated photonic-crystal nanolasers.
why_it_matters: The method provides a compact electrical diagnostic for collective optical locking without requiring separate high-resolution optical readout of each laser.
detailed_summary: Two disorder-detuned photonic-crystal nanolasers coupled to a common silicon waveguide are injection-locked by one master laser. Independent pump modulation at distinct radio frequencies produces a difference-frequency beat note only where the two locking ranges overlap. This RF signature directly maps the simultaneously locked state.
main_result: A difference-frequency beat note appears exclusively when both integrated nanolasers are simultaneously locked to the common master.
application_angle: The diagnostic can aid synchronization, calibration, and control of dense on-chip laser arrays for communications and photonic processing.

title: Cavity-enhanced second harmonic generation from Rydberg excitons in Cu$_2$O
abstract: Rydberg excitons in Cu$_2$O provide a solid-state setting for creating giant optical nonlinearities. Here, we use second-harmonic generation (SHG) to study Rydberg excitons in a doubly resonant optical microcavity designed to enhance both the pump and second-harmonic fields. We observe even-parity exciton states in an optical cavity and extend cavity-based measurements of Rydberg excitons up to $n=10$. The SHG intensity depends strongly on pump cavity detuning, showing the dominant role of the microcavity is the enhancement of the intra-cavity pump field. Analysis reveals an additional enhancement from the resonant second-harmonic cavity giving an overall SHG enhancement factor of $21 \pm 2$ inside the microcavity. These results establish cavity-enhanced SHG spectroscopy as a valuable tool for studying Rydberg excitons in microcavities and provide a pathway towards exploiting optical nonlinearities in Rydberg exciton polariton systems.
one_liner: A doubly resonant microcavity boosts second-harmonic generation from Cu2O Rydberg excitons by 21±2 and resolves states up to n=10.
why_it_matters: The experiment combines cavity enhancement with parity-sensitive nonlinear spectroscopy, advancing strongly interacting solid-state optical platforms.
detailed_summary: The study probes Cu2O Rydberg excitons through second-harmonic generation in a microcavity resonant at both the pump and harmonic frequencies. It observes even-parity states and extends cavity measurements to principal quantum number n=10. Pump-field buildup supplies the dominant enhancement, while harmonic resonance contributes to an overall intracavity SHG enhancement of 21±2.
main_result: Cavity-enhanced SHG resolves even-parity Rydberg excitons through n=10 with an overall enhancement factor of 21±2.
application_angle: The platform supports sensitive exciton spectroscopy and may enable large optical nonlinearities for Rydberg-exciton-polariton quantum devices.

title: Universal photonic synthetic temporal-mode converter for heterogeneous quantum interconnects
abstract: We propose a synthetic temporal-mode converter (STC) that combines programmable waveform matching with denser time multiplexing for heterogeneous quantum interconnects. Programmable couplers and optical delays reshape known single-photon temporal waveforms through coherent interference between time bins. Conversion to a common single-bin mode concentrates amplitudes from $N$ bins in $\lceil\log_2N\rceil$ mixing stages, simultaneously improving temporal indistinguishability and freeing channel time. Simulations yield mode overlaps above 99.9\% for exponential and Gaussian inputs. For $N=256$ and $0.5\,\mathrm{dB}$ loss per stage, STC gives a 45.6-fold higher photon-pair coincidence rate than temporal gating at equal mode overlap for two exponential inputs. Relative to long pulses, the shortened temporal matched mode can support an approximately 41-fold higher photon-pair coincidence rate when the available time-multiplexing capacity is fully utilized.
one_liner: A programmable temporal-mode converter coherently compresses diverse single-photon waveforms into a shared time bin with simulated overlap above 99.9%.
why_it_matters: It addresses both waveform mismatch and low time-channel utilization, two central obstacles to linking heterogeneous quantum nodes.
detailed_summary: The proposed converter uses programmable couplers and optical delays to interfere amplitudes from N temporal bins and concentrate them into one matched bin in ⌈log2N⌉ stages. Simulations exceed 99.9% overlap for exponential and Gaussian inputs. For N=256 with 0.5 dB loss per stage, it predicts 45.6 times the coincidence rate of temporal gating at equal overlap and about 41 times that of long-pulse matching under full multiplexing.
main_result: The simulated architecture achieves over 99.9% mode overlap while delivering up to 45.6-fold higher coincidence rates than temporal gating.
application_angle: It could connect quantum emitters with dissimilar photon envelopes while increasing entanglement-generation throughput in multiplexed networks.

title: Scalable Unitary State-Encoding for Generic Large Data
abstract: Efficient encoding of data into quantum states remains a fundamental bottleneck in many quantum computing protocols, which would otherwise offer advantages over their classical counterparts. Here, we introduce deterministic and scalable amplitude-encoding methods with low two-qubit gate costs and tunable trade-offs between circuit depth and encoding fidelity. Our approaches require no amplitude amplification or mid-circuit measurement and are capable of encoding arbitrary complex data or queryable functions by using tensor-networks to go beyond what can be held in classical memory. Our principle contributions are two complementary algorithms for simplifying fully controlled multiplexer circuits to one- and two-qubit gates. In the first, we formally map the elimination of redundant gate controls to a Boolean logic minimization problem, while in the second we utilize a single ancilla qubit to map the multi-controlled rotation gates to a sequence of one- and two-qubit operations via the Walsh-Hadamard spectrum of the gate angles. We benchmark these methods across a broad range of function classes, characterizing their total depth in an all-to-all connectivity graph against system size and target fidelity. Hybridizing our methods gives up to orders of magnitude improvement in circuit depth at equivalent state fidelity compared to the default state-preparation method in the Qiskit package. We furthermore demonstrate our method on IQM hardware with a square lattice connectivity, finding excellent fidelity, even with minimal noise mitigation. By significantly reducing gate depth for encoding, this work enables the experimental execution of applications on current and near-term hardware which would otherwise be reduced to noise before the first calculation step, shortening the time horizon to robust quantum utility.
one_liner: Tensor-network-assisted amplitude encoding cuts state-preparation depth by up to orders of magnitude and is demonstrated on IQM superconducting hardware.
why_it_matters: Lower-depth loading of arbitrary complex data makes more of a noisy quantum processor's coherence budget available for the actual algorithm.
detailed_summary: The work introduces deterministic amplitude-encoding schemes that simplify controlled multiplexers through Boolean control minimization or a single-ancilla Walsh-Hadamard construction. The methods handle arbitrary complex data and queryable functions, using tensor networks when datasets exceed classical memory. Hybrid variants reduce circuit depth by up to orders of magnitude relative to Qiskit's default preparation at comparable fidelity and perform with high fidelity on square-lattice IQM hardware.
main_result: The hybrid encoder achieves up to orders-of-magnitude circuit-depth reductions at equivalent fidelity and is validated experimentally on IQM hardware.
application_angle: Shallower state preparation can make data-intensive quantum algorithms executable on current noisy processors before decoherence dominates.

title: Differentiable Digital Twins for Optimization, Calibration, and Characterization of Neutral-Atom- and Ion-based Quantum Computers
abstract: Quantum technologies based on individually controlled atoms are among the most promising platforms for scalable quantum computing, owing to their favorable coherence properties and controllability. Nonetheless, achieving reliable and high-fidelity gate operations remains challenging due to the sensitivity of these systems to noise and hardware imperfections. In this work, we introduce a comprehensive software toolset designed to model atomic quantum systems with high precision and simulate qubit gate dynamics. By integrating quantum optimal control and benchmarking techniques with automatic differentiation for efficient and accurate gradient-based optimization, the toolset enables significant improvements in gate performance. We demonstrate its capabilities through detailed case studies involving both neutral atoms and trapped ions, highlighting its effectiveness in enhancing quantum gate fidelities, and providing valuable insights for experimental implementation.
one_liner: Differentiable digital twins combine atomic-system simulation, optimal control, and benchmarking to improve neutral-atom and trapped-ion gates.
why_it_matters: Automatic gradients can accelerate calibration and expose hardware imperfections that limit gate fidelity in individually controlled atomic processors.
detailed_summary: The software toolset models atomic quantum systems and simulates qubit-gate dynamics with automatic differentiation. It integrates gradient-based quantum optimal control and benchmarking for optimization, calibration, and characterization. Case studies on neutral-atom and trapped-ion systems show improved gate fidelities and yield experimentally relevant insight into noise and imperfections.
main_result: Differentiable simulation and optimal control improve modeled gate performance across both neutral-atom and trapped-ion case studies.
application_angle: The framework can shorten experimental calibration cycles and support hardware-aware pulse design for higher-fidelity atomic quantum computers.

title: Trajectory-Dependent Decoherence and Leakage During Shuttling of Multi-Spin Qubits
abstract: Logical qubits encoded in collective states of multiple spins are promising building blocks for large-scale semiconductor quantum processors. As novel fault-tolerant architectures increasingly rely on qubit shuttling, understanding decoherence of the shuttled multi-spin qubits becomes crucial. We analyze fidelity and leakage of the logical qubits dephased by the spatio-temporally correlated $1/f$ noise, considering two-, three-, and four-spin encodings. We study different shuttling protocols and establish that for all encodings generally, parallel shuttling provides the best protection against decoherence at short distances, whereas sequential shuttling outperforms others for long-range transport (although the exact boundaries depend on the specific device parameters). We explain this common behavior in terms of the dephasing factors of pairs of the shuttled spins; we provide explicit expressions for fidelities and leakage, thus enabling experimentalists to predict performance of the multi-spin qubits from only several independently measured pairwise dephasing factors. Our results establish a connection between shuttling trajectories, noise correlations, and qubit decoherence, and provide guidance for achieving noise-resilient shuttling in scalable semiconductor quantum processors.
one_liner: Shuttling trajectories determine decoherence and leakage in multi-spin logical qubits exposed to correlated 1/f noise.
why_it_matters: The results provide experimentally accessible rules for selecting noise-resilient qubit-transport protocols in scalable semiconductor processors.
detailed_summary: The study analyzes fidelity and logical-state leakage for two-, three-, and four-spin encodings shuttled through spatiotemporally correlated 1/f noise. Parallel shuttling generally minimizes decoherence over short distances, while sequential shuttling performs better for long-range transport, with crossover points set by device parameters. Explicit formulas reduce multi-spin performance prediction to several independently measurable pairwise dephasing factors.
main_result: Trajectory-dependent analysis identifies parallel shuttling as generally optimal at short range and sequential shuttling as superior for long-range transport.
application_angle: Pairwise dephasing measurements can guide transport-protocol selection and device optimization for scalable fault-tolerant semiconductor quantum processors.

title: What is the connection between quantum relationality and symmetry-based relationality?
abstract: Although it has often been noted that both quantum mechanics and relativistic physics involve significant forms of relationality, the nature of the connection remains unclear. In addressing such a question it makes sense to start from the simplest possibility, so in this article I set out to consider the viability of the hypothesis that the two types of relationality are ultimately the same: that is, quantum states always characterize degrees of freedom which can be changed by a symmetry transformation, so they are relativized for exactly the same reason as partial observables in general relativity. I use the idea that we only measure partial observables to argue that this suggestion is compatible with all existing empirical evidence for quantum mechanics, and then I consider the consequences for ongoing debates about the nature of measurement in quantum mechanics.
one_liner: The paper explores whether quantum and symmetry-based relationality share a common origin in symmetry-transformable degrees of freedom.
why_it_matters: It offers a unified perspective on relational observables and the quantum measurement problem.

title: Nondestructive 3D Metrology of Through-Glass Via Geometry and Internal Wall Texture Using Holotomography
abstract: Through-glass vias (TGVs) are increasingly important for semiconductor packaging, yet their internal geometry and wall texture remain difficult to characterize nondestructively. Here, we use holotomography (HT) to inspect the three-dimensional (3D) geometry and internal wall texture of intact, unfilled TGVs before metallization. HT reconstructs the refractive index (RI) distribution of the glass and via. Maps of RI and spatially filtered RI then localize the internal boundary. Geometric fitting quantifies via dimensions and taper, while spatial filtering separates slowly varying wall form from finer texture. The reconstructed surface supports volumetric visualization, dimensional measurements and spatial characterization of wall texture within one optical inspection workflow. These measurements reveal internal features inaccessible from surface views and provide quantitative descriptors to evaluate TGVs
one_liner: Holotomography nondestructively reconstructs through-glass via geometry and separates wall form from fine internal texture.
why_it_matters: The method enables quantitative inspection of intact vias before metallization without destructive sectioning.

title: Quantum Temporal Marginal Problem
abstract: Experiments on a multi-time quantum process may reveal its responses only on selected, possibly overlapping, sets of times. We ask whether these partial descriptions admit a common underlying process, and formulate this process tensor marginal problem as a semidefinite feasibility test. Agreement on overlaps is necessary but insufficient: three locally consistent qubit marginals can have no common extension. Another family is incompatible as a time-ordered process even though a single quantum channel satisfies both its channel and temporal marginal constraints. This isolates temporal causality as the obstruction. We quantify incompatibility by the mixing needed to restore compatibility and derive finite tests using separate interventions at each time and final measurements. We further show that incompatibility is equivalent to an advantage over every compatible family in a multi-time process-discrimination task. Together, these results test whether process descriptions obtained in different experiments can arise from one causally ordered quantum process.
one_liner: A semidefinite test determines whether overlapping temporal marginals can arise from one causally ordered quantum process.
why_it_matters: It distinguishes simple marginal inconsistency from incompatibility caused specifically by temporal causality.

title: Lieb-Robinson bounds for Bose-Hubbard Hamiltonians via path expansions
abstract: We study the transport properties of Bose-Hubbard-type Hamiltonians. Kuwahara, Vu, and Saito proved sharp bounds on (i) particle transport and (ii) the Lieb-Robinson velocity for initial states with controlled boson density. We provide simpler and shorter proofs for both results using a new set of methods. For (i), boson transport, we use a class of weighted extended particle number operators that directly enables closing the associated differential inequalities. For (ii), the Lieb-Robinson bounds, we develop a bosonic version of the Chen-Lucas path expansion technique and recover the sharp velocity bound $t^{d-1}$ up to logarithmic corrections, where $d$ denotes the lattice dimension. We also extend the transport bounds (i) to long-range hopping with a power-law exponent $α>d$. The range $α\in (d,d+1)$ corresponds to an algebraic light cone for boson transport and has not been previously covered.
one_liner: Path expansions yield streamlined sharp transport and Lieb–Robinson bounds for Bose–Hubbard systems with controlled density.
why_it_matters: The approach also covers long-range hopping regimes that exhibit algebraic bosonic light cones.

title: Chirality-Induced Angular-Momentum Pumping by Moving Charges
abstract: Chirality-induced spin selectivity is established even in light elements at room temperature; dissipation and electron correlations are implicated, here combined in one mechanism. Injected electron wave packets coherently radiate chiral phonons; electronic absorption competing with phonon decay sets the fraction electrons receive and its temperature dependence. Spin-orbit coupling itself is not renormalized; it becomes effectively large because both the orbital and spin moments it couples are enhanced by Coulomb correlations.
one_liner: Moving electrons radiate chiral phonons that pump angular momentum back into correlated electronic orbital and spin moments.
why_it_matters: The mechanism connects dissipation and correlations to strong room-temperature chirality-induced spin selectivity.

title: The Reference System Loophole
abstract: I argue that the Extended Wigner's Friend theorems have a `loophole' that has previously not been appreciated, coming from the fact that we typically need a reference system to give meaning to a measurement outcome. I show how this loophole can be used in the context of the Local Friendliness theorem to preserve the predictions of quantum mechanics without denying Local Friendliness, and I respond to some objections. I explain how the loophole arises naturally from consideration of relevant symmetry transformations, and then I appeal to the partial/complete observables formalism to argue that the same loophole will work for any type of Wigner's Friend experiment, even if it is performed with a variable that does not obviously look like it requires relativization to a reference system. Finally I compare the loophole to other possible responses to the Local Friendliness theorem, and I show that the same loophole will work for other Extended Wigner's Friend theorems too.
one_liner: Reference-system dependence is proposed as a loophole in Local Friendliness and other extended Wigner’s-friend theorems.
why_it_matters: It presents a route to retain quantum predictions without rejecting Local Friendliness assumptions.

title: Probing non-adiabaticity in a quantum Otto cycle through quantum texture and imaginarity
abstract: Finite-time driving in quantum thermodynamic cycles inevitably generates coherences in the instantaneous energy basis, leading to quantum friction and degrading the operational performance. In this work, we demonstrate that the non-adiabatic inner friction produced during unitary driving of a two-level system can be faithfully quantified by combining two distinct resource-theoretic notions: quantum texture (rugosity) and imaginarity. We show that neither rugosity nor imaginarity alone is sufficient to track the total non-adiabaticity, and we introduce a combined witness, which is strictly non-negative and vanishes if and only if the driving is quasi-static. Applying this framework to a finite-time quantum Otto refrigerator, we establish an exact closed-form relation connecting the coefficient of performance directly to the quantum texture and imaginarity, evaluated at the end of the unitary compression and expansion strokes. Furthermore, we show that local minima of the non-adiabatic witness accurately identify the operating regimes that maximize cooling performance. Our findings provide a geometric and resource-theoretic foundation for inner friction, offering practical diagnostic tools for optimizing finite-time quantum thermal machines.
one_liner: A combined witness based on quantum rugosity and imaginarity exactly tracks nonadiabatic friction in a two-level Otto cycle.
why_it_matters: The witness provides a practical diagnostic for locating high-performance regimes in finite-time quantum refrigerators.

title: Shallow data-loading circuits for multivariable functions
abstract: We construct shallow QROM, diagonal block-encoding, and quantum state preparation oracles for analytic functions on the $D$-dimensional hypercube $[0, 1]^D$. On $n$ qubits and with $2^{- Ω(n/D)}$ error, these circuits have depths of $O \left( \sqrt{\frac{n \log_2 (n)}{D}} \right)$ in the Clifford + $T$ gate set, albeit using $2^{O(\sqrt{nD \log_2 (n)})}$ ancilla qubits. This is a near-quadratic depth reduction compared to known linear-depth methods.
one_liner: Shallow circuits load analytic multivariable functions into QROM, block encodings, and quantum states with near-quadratic depth savings.
why_it_matters: The construction reduces data-loading depth substantially, though at the cost of many ancillary qubits.

title: Optical Detection of Coefficient of Thermal Expansion via Frequency Tracking at Cryogenic Temperatures
abstract: Accurate characterization of the coefficient of thermal expansion (CTE) in nanoscale thin films is critical for predicting residual stress and ensuring the reliability of modern micro-electromechanical systems and advanced semiconductor architectures. The primary limitation is that traditional methods depend on precise thickness measurements or are restricted to crystalline materials. In this work, we present an in-situ, non-destructive optical methodology to determine the CTE of suspended nanofilms by tracking the temperature-dependence of their vibrational frequency. This approach eliminates thickness measurements entirely and works for amorphous films where X-ray diffraction (XRD) fails. We experimentally validate this technique across a broad temperature range, evaluating membranes in their native microstructure state without requiring additional destructive patterning or complex sample preparation. This non-contact optical method achieves uncertainty below 5.3 * 10-8 K-1, substantially improving upon conventional thin-film CTE metrology.
one_liner: An optical method extracts cryogenic thin-film thermal expansion from a suspended membrane’s temperature-dependent vibration frequency.
why_it_matters: It avoids thickness measurements and destructive preparation while supporting amorphous nanofilms.

title: Quantum simulation of dissipative acoustic and elastic waves by Schrödingerisation: absorbing boundaries and explicit polynomial-size circuits
abstract: Explicit quantum circuits for the acoustic and elastic wave equations, obtained by Hamiltonian simulation of their first-order forms, conserve energy and therefore describe closed domains: an outgoing wave reflects off the edge of the computational region or, with periodic boundaries, wraps around and re-enters from the opposite side. We open the domain with the simplest physical absorber, a graded sponge layer in which every wave field is damped at a rate that grows towards the outer edge, and implement the resulting dissipative dynamics on a quantum simulator by Schrödingerisation, which turns a non-unitary linear evolution into a family of unitary ones by means of a single auxiliary variable. We derive the whole chain from the partial differential equation to the circuit, in one, two and three dimensions. An independent finite-difference solver confirms that damping all wave fields absorbs far better than the common velocity-only damping mask. For the sponge the quantum analysis is sharp: recovery is exact on the whole non- negative half of the auxiliary axis at every time; that axis can be truncated periodically at a length set by the largest damping rate and the simulated time; and the success probability is a fixed constant, about 0.4, times the fraction of the energy not yet absorbed, with only one or two auxiliary qubits measured. On the circuit side, the damping step, which generic synthesis compiles into a number of controlled-NOT gates exponential in the number of qubits, factorises exactly into polynomially many multi-controlled phase gates. Gate-level simulations on up to 25 qubits agree with the classical solutions of the damped wave equations.
one_liner: Schrödingerisation enables dissipative quantum simulations of acoustic and elastic waves with absorbing sponge boundaries.
why_it_matters: Exact factorization replaces exponential generic damping synthesis with polynomial-size circuit components.

title: State Synthesis with an NP oracle
abstract: In this note, I describe a quantum algorithm that prepares an arbitrary state $|ψ\rangle$ to inverse exponential precision in polynomial time by making queries to an $\mathsf{NP}$ oracle, assuming one can directly query entries of the state vector corresponding to $|ψ\rangle$. The previous best upper bound on the complexity class required by an oracle for this task was $\mathsf{PP}$. I provide evidence that $\mathsf{NP}$ is the best possible upper bound by showing that any quantum algorithm using a $\mathsf{P}$ oracle, or even a $\mathsf{P/poly}$ oracle, requires exponentially many queries. I also discuss some implications of this result for the $\mathsf{QMA}$ search-to-decision problem and unitary synthesis.
one_liner: An NP-oracle quantum algorithm prepares arbitrary query-accessible states to inverse-exponential precision in polynomial time.
why_it_matters: It improves the prior PP-oracle upper bound and gives evidence that NP is essentially optimal.

title: Nearly Transform-Limited Pulse-Like Temporal and Narrowband Spectral Responses in Sum-Frequency Generation from Bright Twin Beams
abstract: We simultaneously characterize the temporal and spectral responses of the coherent component in bright twin beams using a spectrally resolved, delay-dependent sum-frequency generation (SFG) measurement. The measured temporal-correlation width is 0.138 ps, close to the transform-limited value of 0.126 ps estimated from the measured twin-beam spectrum.The observed spectral-correlation width is 0.176 rad/ps and is limited by the spectrometer resolution. The corresponding time-frequency width product is 0.0243, far below the value of 1 for SFG between two independent transform-limited Gaussian pulses.
one_liner: Delay-resolved sum-frequency generation reveals nearly transform-limited temporal and narrowband spectral correlations in bright twin beams.
why_it_matters: The unusually small time-frequency width product demonstrates strong joint temporal-spectral coherence.

title: Conditional stopping guarantees for a folded parametrization of reduced Stokes vectors
abstract: Stopping decisions made in parametrization coordinates need not certify physically accurate estimates. We establish conditional stopping guarantees for a folded parametrization of reduced Stokes vectors, including partial linear polarization. For strongly convex physical objectives on the bounded-intensity inner sheet, normalized first derivatives and one radial lower-curvature test give an explicit objective-gap bound with sharp tolerance orders $\varepsilon^{4/3}+ν^2$. The guarantee requires neither prior localization near an optimum nor a positive-semidefinite head Hessian. Its information basis is an exact recovery identity: one signed radial curvature restores the physical-gradient component lost at the fully linearly polarized fold, without stationarity or knowledge of the physical Hessian. For a nominal quadratic model, an outward-rounded implementation certifies a gap of at most $10^{-6}$ for 8,861 of 9,284 stored endpoints; it rejects all 295 historical false successes and 128 accurate endpoints. The full 128-fractional-bit pass takes 7.32 seconds and includes 52 scalar curvature evaluations. Controlled fits and released observations distinguish stopping certification from local fold diagnosis and subsequent coordinate repair. Twenty shared-network fits contain no saved near-fold negative-curvature candidates, and direct physical solvers are cheaper on the tested quadratics.
one_liner: A folded Stokes-vector parametrization gains explicit conditional stopping bounds from normalized gradients and one radial curvature test.
why_it_matters: It prevents coordinate-based stopping rules from falsely certifying inaccurate polarization estimates.

title: Finite attainment and efficient computation of regularized quantum channel relative entropy
abstract: Quantum channel relative entropy can be nonadditive, making its regularization essential for asymptotic analysis. We study when the regularized value is attained at finite blocklength and how efficiently it can be approximated. For the first question, we establish a sharp dichotomy: the regularized value is either attained already at the single-copy level, implying additivity at every blocklength, or is never attained at any finite blocklength. Notably, a simple two-copy additivity test distinguishes between these alternatives for qubit channels and for channel pairs in arbitrary dimensions admitting an interior optimizer. We further show that both the interiority condition and finite nonattainment are generic, holding for almost every channel pair. For the second question, we establish explicit convergence rates for approximating the regularized channel relative entropy. For fixed channel dimensions, $\widetilde O(\varepsilon^{-3/2})$ channel copies suffice to approximate the regularized value to additive accuracy $\varepsilon$. Alternatively, a semidefinite hierarchy achieves the same accuracy at level $\widetilde O(\varepsilon^{-2})$, yielding a certified polynomial-time approximation. Together, these results reveal the intriguing structure and generic behavior of regularized channel relative entropy, sharpening our understanding of both its analytical and computational aspects.
one_liner: Regularized quantum channel relative entropy is either single-copy additive or unattainable at every finite blocklength.
why_it_matters: The dichotomy and approximation bounds clarify both asymptotic channel theory and practical computation.

title: Coupled Soft-Clamped Polygon Resonators with Tunable Mechanical Coupling
abstract: Coupler geometry controls both the frequency splitting and the dissipation of coupled polygon resonators. We develop a continuum model for two identical square-shaped resonators coupled by a shared tether and compare the analytical predictions with finite element simulations. The model relates the coupler length and width to the frequency splitting and dissipation dilution of the two coupled modes. In the short-coupler limit, $k_cl_c\ll1$, the symmetric-mode coupler undergoes nearly uniform rotation, and its torsional strain energy vanishes asymptotically. The remaining loss contributions arise from polygon-side bending and supporting-tether torsion. The reduced supporting-tether contribution allows the symmetric-mode dissipation dilution to exceed that of an isolated polygon with the same side and supporting-tether dimensions. The antisymmetric mode retains torsional strain in the coupler and has an additional loss contribution. We also derive an expression for $Q\cdot f$ in the short-coupler and short-tether limits, where $Q$ is the mechanical quality factor and $f$ is the resonance frequency. This expression gives the dependence of $Q\cdot f$ on tensile stress, film thickness, and supporting-tether geometry. For a coupler length of $100~μ\mathrm{m}$ and width of $2~μ\mathrm{m}$, finite element calculations give a frequency splitting of $17.7~\mathrm{Hz}$ and a symmetric-mode dilution factor approximately $13\%$ above the analytical isolated-polygon value.
one_liner: A continuum model links shared-tether geometry to mode splitting and dissipation in coupled soft-clamped polygon resonators.
why_it_matters: It provides design rules for tunable coupling while preserving or enhancing mechanical quality factors.

title: Logarithmic Bias of Zero-Noise Extrapolation under 1/f Noise
abstract: Zero-noise extrapolation estimates ideal quantum observables by amplifying noise and extrapolating the measured response. Its accuracy depends on whether the extrapolation model captures the physical effect of amplification, including correlations between repeated operations. Here we derive the response of complete multiqubit gate folding in the simultaneous presence of time-local Markovian noise and stationary finite-band 1/f noise. An ordered circuit kernel couples the observable to noise memory; exact block counting shows how folding samples correlations at increasing time separations. The resulting response contains an r^2 ln r coordinate, with a coefficient fixed by the noise spectrum and the integrated forward-inverse control response. Ordinary polynomial Richardson extrapolation leaves a calculable contribution from this coordinate; the three-node rule (1,3,5) retains 2.73 theta. We construct response-matched extrapolation, including a log-domain implementation, that cancels this contribution at the retained order. Explicit bounds separate the remaining control-shape, finite-band, higher-order, and native-offset errors. The theory applies to arbitrary finite multiqubit circuits within the stated control and noise model, and distinguishes removal of memory-induced bias from an unconditional guarantee of the ideal intercept. Single- and ten-qubit numerical examples illustrate the predicted correction and its response dependence.
one_liner: Finite-band 1/f noise adds an r² ln r response term that biases ordinary Richardson zero-noise extrapolation.
why_it_matters: Response-matched extrapolation can remove a memory-induced bias missed by standard polynomial models.

title: Dual-Space Analysis of Vortex Configurations and Rotational Energy in a 2D Optical Lattice
abstract: We investigate the effects of a stationary two-dimensional periodic optical lattice on a rotating Bose--Einstein condensate confined by an isotropic harmonic trap. Within the mean-field description, the condensate is modeled by the two-dimensional Gross--Pitaevskii equation in the rotating frame and solved numerically using an imaginary-time split-step Crank--Nicolson method to obtain stationary vortex states. We examine how the lattice depth, lattice wave vector, particle number, and angular velocity influence the vortex configurations, real-space density, momentum-space density, and energetics of the condensate. We find that the stationary periodic lattice significantly modifies vortex nucleation and spatial organization: vortices emerge progressively with increasing angular velocity and, for sufficiently strong lattice strength, undergo rearrangement and merging. Importantly, changes in the vortex configuration are directly reflected in the momentum-space density, demonstrating that vortex nucleation and rearrangement produce pronounced modifications of the condensate momentum distribution. We further analyze the energy per particle and rotational energy as functions of the angular velocity and find that the presence of the optical lattice substantially alters the rotational response of the condensate. In particular, the rotational energy is progressively reduced at higher angular velocities as the lattice strength is increased. These results demonstrate how a stationary periodic optical lattice modifies vortex formation, momentum-space structure, and rotational energetics of a rotating trapped Bose--Einstein condensate.
one_liner: Simulations show how a stationary optical lattice reshapes vortices, momentum distributions, and rotational energy in a rotating condensate.
why_it_matters: Momentum-space signatures offer a route to observing lattice-driven vortex nucleation and rearrangement.

title: Dynamical-mean-field cluster-correlation expansion of NV$^-$ spin-echo decoherence in a realistic substitutional-nitrogen bath
abstract: The Hahn-echo time $T_2$ of nitrogen-vacancy (NV$^-$) ensembles in nitrogen-rich diamond follows the empirical relation $T_2\cdot$[N] = 160 $μ$s ppm, and this relation does not depend on the magnetic field between 2 and 30 mT. Cluster-correlation-expansion (CCE) calculations solve the spin dynamics exactly within small groups of spins. When they treat the Overhauser field of the surrounding P1 centres, that is, the field that these electron spins produce, as frozen, they overestimate $T_2$ at high field by up to a factor of two. This excess was recently attributed to additional dark defects. We show that the excess comes mostly from the frozen field. In our model the P1 centres outside each cluster flip-flop in pairs: two centres exchange their spin states and conserve their total $S_z$. Kinetic Monte Carlo generates these events at golden-rule rates, which follow from the dipolar Hamiltonian without adjustable parameters, and each cluster evolves in the resulting time-dependent field. This dynamical mean field lies between the static-mean-field and mean-field-free limits. For a $^{14}$N P1 bath it reduces $T_2\cdot$[N] at 30 mT from 264 $\pm$ 16 to 188 $\pm$ 12 $μ$s ppm and gives 167 $\pm$ 11 $μ$s ppm at 10 mT, 1.7 and 0.4 standard deviations from experiment, with no dark spins. When each centre jumps independently, $T_2\cdot$[N] is 147 $\pm$ 9 $μ$s ppm at 30 mT; the correlation of the flip-flop partners thus lengthens $T_2$ by 20-30 percent at high field. The Overhauser field is neither frozen nor averaged out by fast motion: 68-83 percent of its autocorrelation survives 200 $μ$s. At 2.5 mT, where the P1 electron and nucleus hybridise, $T_2$ stays below experiment for any choice of rates. Part of the field dependence therefore remains: $T_2$ rises by a factor 1.69 $\pm$ 0.07 instead of 2.15 $\pm$ 0.08 from 2.5 to 30 mT.
one_liner: A dynamical-mean-field CCE attributes much of the high-field NV spin-echo discrepancy to correlated P1-bath flip-flops.
why_it_matters: It approaches measured NV ensemble coherence without invoking additional dark spin defects.

title: Deterministic and dynamic synthesis of optical skyrmions through an ultrathin multimode fibre
abstract: Topological light fields offer powerful opportunities for information encoding, transport, and manipulation, yet their deterministic generation in complex scattering media remains an outstanding challenge. In highly multimode fibres, strong mode coupling and polarisation mixing can obscure the precise control required to synthesise structured vectorial states, including optical skyrmions. Here, we demonstrate the deterministic generation and dynamic reconfiguration of arbitrary optical skyrmions through an ultrathin multimode fibre. By combining vectorial transmission-matrix control with a phase-retrieval optimisation framework, we exploit the full polarisation-resolved modal space of the fibre to reconstruct user-defined vector fields with high fidelity at the distal facet. This approach enables the synthesis of Néel, Bloch, anti- and higher-order skyrmions, and bimerons. Their topological properties are confirmed through polarisation-resolved Stokes-vector measurements and quantitative determination of the skyrmion number. Wavefront reprogramming further provides dynamic control over polarisation textures, enabling reversible transitions between distinct skyrmionic states. Our results establish multimode fibres as programmable platforms for the generation of topological light and introduce a scalable route towards minimally invasive topological photonics, with potential applications in imaging, sensing, optical communications, and information processing in complex environments.
one_liner: Vectorial transmission control enables deterministic, reconfigurable synthesis of multiple optical-skyrmion classes through an ultrathin multimode fibre.
why_it_matters: It turns multimode fibres into programmable platforms for minimally invasive topological photonics.

title: Chiral phonon magnetism from localized Raman excitation
abstract: Optically driven chiral phonons can induce transient magnetism in non-magnetic crystals, yet the microscopic relationship between phonon angular momentum and the resulting magnetic response remains unresolved. Here we distinguish the roles of pseudo-angular momentum and mechanical angular momentum in tetragonal α-TeO2. Combining phase-resolved terahertz spectroscopy with magneto-optical Kerr measurements (MOKE), we reconstruct the motion of a doubly degenerate phonon and continuously control its angular momentum. The MOKE response follows the sign and magnitude of phonon angular momentum as well as its dynamics, whereas non-rotating phonons, including those with finite pseudo-angular momentum, produce no detectable magnetic signal. The MOKE rotation corresponds to an effective magnetic field of approximately 14 mT, nearly seven orders of magnitude above the estimate for spatially uniform ionic currents. Moreover, the Kerr response scales linearly with the emitted terahertz field, rather than quadratically as predicted by the uniform-current model. A localized Raman-excitation model involving Te lone-pair states accounts for this scaling and yields a comparable field magnitude with the MOKE data when electronic enhancement is included. These findings identify mechanical lattice rotation as the dominant dynamical variable for the observed magnetic response and suggest that localized Raman coupling contributes to its unexpectedly large magnitude.
one_liner: Phase-resolved measurements link transient magnetism in α-TeO₂ to mechanical chiral-phonon rotation rather than pseudo-angular momentum.
why_it_matters: The results identify the relevant lattice motion and suggest why phonon-driven magnetic fields are unexpectedly large.

title: Physics-Informed Surrogate for Sb2S3 Dispersion Trimming in Thin-Film Lithium Niobate
abstract: A film-thickness error of 8 nm, within the tolerance of commercial thin-film lithium niobate wafers, shifts the group-velocity dispersion $β_2$ at 1550 nm by about 28 ps$^2$ km$^{-1}$. We study numerically whether a segmented, non-volatile phase-change cladding can correct this error after fabrication. In mode solves of 3012 geometries, Sb$_2$S$_3$ switches $β_2$ by a median of 181 ps$^2$ km$^{-1}$ at a 40 nm strip thickness with no material absorption under the adopted optical constants, whereas Sb$_2$Se$_3$ reaches a comparable contrast at a median modal loss of 5.6 dB cm$^{-1}$. Because phase adds along the guide, four independently switched binary segments reach a two-dimensional region of the $(β_2,β_3)$ plane; eigenmode expansion supports this description at the junctions. Full-wave solves at 65 die geometries show that the segment states move with the die error, so the bit pattern is chosen from a per-die model: a spectral surrogate constrained by exact identities of the lossless Maxwell problem. Its accuracy within the training domain is similar to that of unconstrained baselines; it keeps $β_2$ and $β_3$ consistent, and its error at an unseen film thickness is 8.3 rather than 13.0 ps$^2$ km$^{-1}$. With a bare test ring and a second ring carrying a crystalline strip already on the mask, 96.8% of the dies are trimmed into $\pm25$ ps$^2$ km$^{-1}$, scored on full-wave solutions. A thermal model gives a candidate write window for a 532 nm beam.
one_liner: A physics-constrained surrogate selects segmented Sb₂S₃ cladding states to trim dispersion errors in thin-film lithium-niobate devices.
why_it_matters: Post-fabrication correction could improve photonic yield despite wafer-thickness variations.

title: Edge photocurrent distribution in luminescent solar concentrators: analytical treatment and solar cell arrangement
abstract: In luminescent solar concentrators (LSCs), the light flux along the edges is non-uniform, which causes current mismatch between series-connected edge solar cells. Here, the optical path distribution of photons arriving at an edge point was derived analytically for a rectangular LSC and generalized to convex polygons, with reabsorption and scattering included as a geometric series. The model agrees with Monte Carlo simulations and reproduces measured edge cell currents of a $60\times60$ cm$^2$ LSC within 2-3%. In a square LSC, the series mismatch reduces the current by 8-12% for four cells per edge. Rules for edge solar cell arrangement are formulated.
one_liner: An analytical photon-path model predicts nonuniform edge photocurrent and series mismatch in polygonal luminescent solar concentrators.
why_it_matters: The model enables better edge-cell layouts and matches measured currents within 2–3%.

title: Entanglement inference from quantum erasure and path discrimination
abstract: Fringes recovered by conditioning on quantum-eraser outcomes do not, by themselves, establish entanglement. We determine the minimum entanglement compatible with recorded eraser data when the preparation may be mixed, distinguishing these data from independently determined optimal which-path distinguishabilities and additional joint measurement outcomes. For noisy Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger (GHZ) preparations, explicit compatible states establish sharp entanglement-depth thresholds and show how parity information strengthens certification. A matching converse establishes the exact threshold for two complete Pauli-outcome distributions. For an ideal three-qubit eraser, we classify the additional marker measurement directions that certify genuine multipartite entanglement within a fixed eraser configuration and determine the separate minima of compatible concurrence and squared GHZ fidelity for specified tilted axes. For noisy three-qubit data, an exact semidefinite characterization and constructive converse determine biseparable compatibility at arbitrary fixed local measurement axes, with rational certificates bounding one example. These results establish what entanglement is required by the measurement record, rather than inferred from assumptions about the source.
one_liner: Compatibility bounds determine the minimum entanglement required by quantum-eraser, path-discrimination, and auxiliary measurement data.
why_it_matters: They separate genuine data-driven entanglement certification from assumptions about the prepared source.

title: Phase-locked beam splitting with continuously tunable intensity ratio using stochastic phase masks
abstract: We introduce a common-path beam splitter based on a randomly partitioned phase mask displayed on a spatial light modulator (SLM). The SLM aperture is divided into square patches, each randomly assigned to one of three phase ramps that steer light to three independent foci: two phase-locked beams and a dump that takes up the surplus power. We observe the beams in the focal plane of a lens. The fractions of patches assigned to each ramp set the focal intensities, with the focus positions controlled by the ramp slopes.We first demonstrate experimentally that the intensity ratio between the two foci can be tuned from 0 to 1 without distorting either of the spatial modes, and with their relative phase constant to within a few tens of mrad. We then derive a closed-form expression for the ensemble-averaged focal intensity, which decomposes into coherent foci of the desired pattern and a speckle background whose shape and amplitude are set by the patch size. The model is validated against experiment and against numerical Fraunhofer propagation, with quantitative agreement over about three orders of magnitude in intensity. We also identify the patch size as the central design parameter and characterize its experimental bounds.
one_liner: A stochastic three-ramp SLM mask creates two phase-locked beams with continuously tunable power sharing and an adjustable dump channel.
why_it_matters: It offers common-path intensity control without spatial-mode distortion or substantial relative-phase drift.

title: Quantized pumping of boundary Hilbert space in chiral Floquet phases
abstract: Chiral Floquet phases support quantized chiral flow along their boundaries even when the bulk is fully localized. In this Letter, we establish a complementary phenomenon, which we call Hilbert-space pumping: under a boundary condition twisted by time translation, a part of the boundary Hilbert space, of quantized dimension, is transferred between the opposite boundaries. The twist is the temporal analogue of Laughlin's flux insertion in the quantum Hall effect. For noninteracting fermions, the number of transferred boundary modes is determined by the winding number, as we show analytically for the boundary dynamics and numerically for the anomalous Floquet Anderson insulator. For interacting systems whose boundary dynamics is a quantum cellular automaton, the transferred dimension is set by the Gross-Nesme-Vogts-Werner (GNVW) index: the twisted boundary Floquet operator is the Floquet operator on a tilted time slice, whose Hilbert-space dimension is multiplied by the index for each period of twist. We derive this relation for matrix product unitaries and test it numerically in random unitary circuits. Applied to the matrix product operators of non-invertible symmetries, the same twisted rank returns the quantum dimension of the symmetry operator in addition to its flow index.
one_liner: Time-translation twists pump a quantized dimension of boundary Hilbert space between opposite edges of chiral Floquet systems.
why_it_matters: It links boundary-state transfer to winding numbers, the GNVW index, and quantum dimensions of non-invertible symmetries.

title: Coulomb Blockade in a One-Dimensional Array of Strong Josephson Junctions
abstract: We measure current across a voltage-biased, long array of Josephson junctions. Current-voltage characteristics do not reveal any critical current and instead display the presence of threshold voltage and finite activation energy, consistent with the Coulomb blockade. However, the respective energy scale is well below the value prescribed by a single-island geometric capacitances. We explain it by strong quantum fluctuations of charge associated with a large value of Josephson energy, $E_J\gg E_C$, where $E_C$ is the charging energy associated with the inter-island capacitance. Comparison between the data and theory points to an exponential (in parameter $E_J/E_C$) suppression of the threshold. We achieve a quantitative agreement with theory by accounting for charge-$e$ solitons associated with the quasiparticles entering the array from its leads. This scenario however underestimates the current below threshold in comparison with the experiment.
one_liner: A long array of strong Josephson junctions exhibits Coulomb blockade with an exponentially suppressed threshold voltage.
why_it_matters: Charge-e solitons explain the measured blockade scale and clarify transport in strongly fluctuating superconducting circuits.

title: unitaryQIP = unitaryPSPACE
abstract: Unitary synthesis complexity studies the computational cost of applying a target unitary to an unknown quantum state, extending complexity theory beyond its traditional focus on problems with classical inputs and outputs. Rosenthal and Yuen (ITCS 2022) introduced two complexity classes for unitary synthesis: $\mathsf{unitaryQIP}$ and $\mathsf{unitaryPSPACE}$ for the unitary families implementable via interactive proofs and in polynomial space, respectively. In this work, we prove the equality $\mathsf{unitaryQIP}=\mathsf{unitaryPSPACE}$ and thereby establish a unitary-complexity analogue of $\mathsf{QIP} = \mathsf{PSPACE}$ (Jain, Ji, Upadhyay, and Watrous, J. ACM 2011) and $\mathsf{stateQIP}=\mathsf{statePSPACE}$ (Rosenthal and Yuen, ITCS 2022; Metger and Yuen, FOCS 2023). To prove $\mathsf{unitaryQIP} \subseteq \mathsf{unitaryPSPACE}$, we use an acceptance rigidity lemma derived from the soundness condition to show that the polynomial-space prover constructed for a fixed input in state synthesis (Metger and Yuen, FOCS 2023) implements the target unitary on every input, leading to a polynomial-space simulation of the protocol. For the reverse inclusion, we build on OpenAI's recently announced solution to the unitary synthesis problem (Aaronson and Kuperberg, Theory Comput. 2007), and show that $\mathsf{unitaryPSPACE}$ families can be synthesized in polynomial time with a $\mathsf{PSPACE}$ oracle. We then implement the oracle queries using auxiliary states prepared via the $\mathsf{statePSPACE} \subseteq \mathsf{stateQIP}$ protocol (Rosenthal and Yuen, ITCS 2022). Beyond the equality, we show that our protocol for $\mathsf{unitaryPSPACE}$ can be parallelized to constant rounds when the verifier receives polynomially many copies of the input, and we also obtain a complexity-theoretic barrier to proving the existence of $\mathsf{EFI}$ pairs.
one_liner: The paper proves that unitary families synthesizable through quantum interactive proofs are exactly those implementable in polynomial space.
why_it_matters: It establishes a unitary-synthesis analogue of QIP = PSPACE and yields constant-round protocols under additional input copies.

title: Reimagining computational quantum research with AI scientists
abstract: AI scientists are expanding automated research across scientific domains, yet their ability to turn the scientific record into a foundation for autonomous discovery remains elusive. Here we uncover a fundamental barrier to this transition and demonstrate a route to overcome it in computational quantum science, where advances shape both what we can learn from complex quantum systems and what quantum computing can ultimately deliver. To identify this barrier, we introduce OmniQ, an expert-audited virtual research environment that converts published studies into executable reproduction tasks. Across 59 papers spanning classical simulation, quantum algorithms and quantum-property characterization, we systematically evaluate five agentic systems powered by large language models and six third-party agent harnesses. Our findings reveal that current AI scientists often fail to reproduce published results, exposing a fundamental mismatch between what scientific papers communicate and what autonomous agents require. By contrast, human expert intervention can turn these failures into successful reproductions, showing that the missing information can be identified and converted into reusable research experience. Guided by this observation, we develop Residual Agents (RA), a quantum-tailored self-improving AI scientist that distils externally verified workflow repairs into such experience. RA substantially improves research performance under fixed base models and limited adaptation budgets. For example, RA raises DeepSeek V4.1 Flash performance from 68% to 85%, matching Claude Code with Opus 5 at a third of its cost despite using a weaker base model. We integrate all reproduced results into an extensible platform built on the model context protocol, making verified research workflows directly accessible to AI scientists and allowing new scientific papers to be continuously incorporated.
one_liner: OmniQ benchmarks AI agents on reproducing 59 quantum-computing papers, while Residual Agents learn reusable repairs from verified failures.
why_it_matters: The results show how expert-verified workflow knowledge can substantially improve autonomous computational research at lower cost.

title: A plug-and-play platform for self-aligning 3D-printed structures on optical fibers
abstract: Two-photon polymerization 3D printing advances optical fibers into complex lab-on-fiber devices. However, widespread adoption remains bottlenecked by the inherent inefficiencies of sequential, direct-on-fiber printing. To address this, a custom-designed modular platform and a corresponding fiber-decoupled fabrication methodology on planar substrates are presented. This platform features a compliant, spring-like socket that enables passive self-alignment and reversible fiber insertion, paired with a customizable frontal device. The shift to fabrication on planar substrates enables parallel batch processing and allows the substrate to serve as a functional magazine for device mounting. To demonstrate this approach, modular platforms featuring a functional tip are printed, sharpened via post-process plasma etching, metallized, and equipped with an optical aperture using focused ion beam milling, while remaining on the planar substrate. Subsequently, these are used as exchangeable scanning probe microscopy tips mounted in situ within a scanning electron microscope. Simultaneous three-channel correlative imaging (atomic force microscopy topography, secondary electron, and cathodoluminescence) is used to validate the optomechanical stability of the design. Ultimately, by decoupling the delicate optical device's lifespan from the optical fiber, this architecture transforms lab-on-fiber tools into scalable, seamlessly replaceable consumables, offering a highly adaptable pathway for broader applications in photonics, sensing, and microscopy.
one_liner: A compliant 3D-printed socket passively aligns replaceable microdevices with optical fibers after scalable planar fabrication.
why_it_matters: The design separates device and fiber lifetimes, enabling batch-made consumables for photonics, sensing, and multimodal microscopy.

title: Quantum-Nondemolition Probing of Multiphoton Transitions between Dressed States in a Strongly Driven Jaynes--Cummings System
abstract: The response of the Jaynes--Cummings (JC) model to strong driving has been examined previously, but the origin of intriguing features near emitter--cavity resonance remains poorly understood because of the large background in conventional transmission spectroscopy. Here we introduce a spectroscopic approach for circuit quantum electrodynamics that combines strong cavity driving with quantum-nondemolition qubit readout. Separating the drive and readout substantially enhances the measurement sensitivity as compared with conventional cavity-transmission spectroscopy. With this technique, we identify the near-resonant features as multiphoton transitions between emitter--photon dressed states of the same parity, and resolve transitions between dressed states of opposite parity. Away from resonance, we also observe selective enhancement and suppression of multiphoton transitions, together with transitions involving the second excited state of the anharmonic qubit. Our approach opens a route to resolving the rich transition structure of the JC ladder and probing strongly driven light--matter interactions.
one_liner: Quantum-nondemolition qubit readout resolves multiphoton transitions across the dressed-state ladder of a strongly driven Jaynes–Cummings system.
why_it_matters: Separating strong drive from readout exposes transition structures hidden by the background of conventional transmission spectroscopy.

title: Full-Rank Constructions of Explicit Lossless Expanders and Good Small-Set qLTCs
abstract: We construct explicit two-sided lossless expanders whose binary adjacency matrices have full rank, and use them to obtain explicit asymptotically good quantum LDPC codes whose specified X- and Z-check matrices have full row rank and satisfy small-set soundness, or confinement, on a linear range. Our lossless expanders are a variant of those of Hsieh, Lubotzky, Mohanty, Reiner, and Zhang, with a free action of a finite 2-group. Under such an action, injectivity and surjectivity of the adjacency matrix are detected on a fixed-size matrix indexed by vertex orbits. Adding a sparse factor to the gadget at the middle vertices of a single type then enforces full rank, with a controlled loss in expansion. To obtain the 2-group action, we observe that reducing the generators of the Lubotzky-Phillips-Sarnak Ramanujan graphs modulo powers of 2, instead of modulo an odd prime, gives Ramanujan Cayley graphs on finite 2-groups. This construction may be of independent interest. Plugging two such expanders into the balanced product of Lin and Hsieh gives the quantum codes, since full rank of the input graphs is inherited by the check matrices. Our construction supplies the code family sought by Hong, Guo, and Lucas. Applying their analysis, within their framework and under their dynamical assumptions, gives quantum memories whose free-energy density is analytic at every positive temperature and whose guaranteed lifetime is $exp(Ω(N))$ at sufficiently low fixed positive temperature, where N is the blocklength. This improves the previously guaranteed stretched-exponential timescale.
one_liner: Explicit full-rank lossless expanders yield asymptotically good quantum LDPC codes with linearly ranged small-set soundness.
why_it_matters: Under stated dynamical assumptions, the codes support a guaranteed exponential memory lifetime at sufficiently low positive temperature.

title: eigenkit: A Provider-Neutral Quantum Computing Library
abstract: Quantum software ecosystems provide increasingly capable tools for simulation and hardware execution, but differences in programming models, supported features, and backend capabilities can make it difficult to move and systematically compare the same quantum algorithm across execution environments. We introduce eigenkit, a provider-neutral quantum computing library that separates algorithm definition from backend execution through a common circuit representation and provider interface. The library currently supports 12 execution providers spanning simulators and quantum hardware, provides backend-independent gradient computation, and integrates with standard scientific-computing and machine-learning workflows through NumPy, PyTorch, and scikit-learn interfaces. We evaluate the practical relevance of this abstraction across both simulation and quantum hardware. Simulator performance varies substantially with circuit size, structure, batching, and application workload, showing that no single backend is consistently preferable. On quantum hardware, experiments on IBM Heron and IQM Emerald show that which processor is better suited to a given algorithm depends not only on hardware constraints, but also on how well the topology of the quantum algorithm matches the physical connectivity of the processor. These results demonstrate that backend portability is not only a software-design convenience, but can be important for both computational efficiency and quantum execution quality.
one_liner: Eigenkit provides a common circuit and provider interface across 12 simulator and quantum-hardware execution environments.
why_it_matters: Its benchmarks show that portability helps select backends by workload, circuit topology, physical connectivity, and execution quality.

title: Shot-to-shot statistical fluctuations during beam self-cleaning in multimode fibers
abstract: Beam self-cleaning in multimode optical fibers has recently been interpreted within a thermodynamic framework, in which nonlinear propagation drives the optical field towards a statistical equilibrium state. While this interpretation has been supported by measurements of modal populations and entropy, the role of shot-to-shot spatial fluctuations of the output beam has so far remained unexplored. Here, we experimentally show that the transverse output beam profile becomes progressively more reproducible from shot to shot as beam self-cleaning develops. This behavior is consistent with the thermodynamic expectation that relative fluctuations become increasingly small as the system approaches equilibrium.
one_liner: Multimode-fiber beam profiles become increasingly reproducible from shot to shot as nonlinear beam self-cleaning develops.
why_it_matters: The reduced relative fluctuations provide new experimental support for a thermodynamic interpretation of beam self-cleaning.

title: Second-order mean force Gibbs state of fermionic open systems
abstract: Thermodynamics typically assumes that a system in contact with a thermal reservoir relaxes to the Gibbs state, or to the grand canonical Gibbs state when it also exchanges particles. However, this only holds when the coupling is very weak. Beyond this, the expected equilibrium state is the mean force Gibbs (MFG) state, obtained by tracing the reservoir out of the thermal state of the combined system. Despite its relevance, general analytic results for the MFG state have so far been obtained almost exclusively for bosonic reservoirs. Here we derive the grand canonical MFG state to second order in the coupling for a generic fermionic system coupled to a thermal reservoir at arbitrary chemical potential, using the concept of the mode reduced state in order for the fermionic MFG state to be well defined. The correction to the bare Gibbs state separates into particle and hole channels weighted by the empty and occupied reservoir states, related through the Kubo-Martin-Schwinger condition. We apply the result to the resonant level model, two modes coupled to a shared reservoir, and the single impurity Anderson model. For the two modes, the reservoir mediates coherence between modes that do not interact directly, something the bare Gibbs state cannot capture. We verify our results against numerically exact calculations, including real-time dynamics for the interacting model, and find agreement between the static prediction and the dynamical relaxation.
one_liner: A second-order grand-canonical mean-force Gibbs state is derived for generic fermionic systems coupled to thermal reservoirs.
why_it_matters: The framework captures finite-coupling effects such as reservoir-mediated coherence and agrees with exact static and dynamical calculations.

title: On physical origin of Berry connection of free relativistic electrons
abstract: No consensus has been reached on the appropriate operators for the spin and orbital angular momentum of free relativistic electrons. But there is a tendency to believe the existence of a spin-orbit coupling through the Berry connection. Here we show that this is not the case. Because the positive-energy solution of the Dirac equation is associated with the state of the electron, it is reasonable to postulate that only when projected onto the positive-energy subspace can observable operators on the Hilbert space of the Dirac equation represent physical quantities of the electron. On this basis, we find, after mapping the projected operators onto an irreducible representation, that the Berry connection describes the position of a quantum reference point with respect to the laboratory reference frame, relative to which the position of the electron is canonical. The orbital angular momentum of the quantum reference point about the origin of the laboratory reference frame is expressed in terms of the Berry connection. It combines with the canonical orbital angular momentum of the electron about the quantum reference point to give the orbital angular momentum of the electron about the origin of the laboratory reference frame.
one_liner: The Berry connection of a positive-energy Dirac electron is interpreted as the position of a quantum reference point, not spin-orbit coupling.
why_it_matters: This reframing offers a physically consistent decomposition of relativistic electron position and orbital angular momentum.

title: Writing with Near-Field: towards Atomic Resolution in Material Processing
abstract: Direct laser writing with ultra-short pulses is the most flexible route to two- and three-dimensional (2D/3D) material modification, yet its resolution is judged against the optical diffraction limit. This review argues the opposite: the finest, most reproducible modifications come not from shortening the wavelength but from localising the absorber. Through the threshold effect and a transient epsilon-near-zero (ENZ) state - the dielectric-to-metal (Die-Met) state of the excited solid - the deposited energy is confined to a dipole-like nano-seed whose near-field intensity falls as r^-6 (ideal point dipole). The localisation is thus set by the seed size, not the focal wavelength, and the final feature is shaped by the material response: post-pulse heat flow, cavitation and quenching. We show that polarisation controls the anisotropy of deposition: the quasi-static near-field and interface boundary conditions select the writing direction and the modification orientation, down to a single defect. We survey energy-deposition mechanisms from 100 nm to the single-nanometer scale and link them to working engineering: stitch-free large-area patterning and record aspect-ratio (10^3-10^4) dicing and wafering of transparent crystals. Finally, we conjecture guided volumetric deposition, in which laser-inscribed lossy nano-seeds act as antennas that let cavity microwaves anneal the modified nano-volumes from within, as a 2.45 GHz oven heats food through water-dipole absorption. Throughout, atomic resolution is used in a quantum-confined sense and denotes a direction of travel: 10-20 nm features are demonstrated, while deterministic single-defect and single-bond modification remain goals. The thesis is that ultrafast direct write beats diffraction-limited intuition because the material itself forms a transient nanoscale absorber whose near-field and boundary conditions govern energy deposition.
one_liner: This review argues that transient nanoscale absorbers and their near fields—not wavelength alone—set ultrafast laser-writing resolution.
why_it_matters: The framework connects nanoscale energy localization and polarization control to precision patterning, dicing, and future defect engineering.

title: Correlated Catalysis Removes the Strong Converse for Entanglement Distillation
abstract: Entanglement distillation converts noisy shared quantum states into maximally entangled pairs using local operations and classical communication. The distillable entanglement $E_D$ determines the maximum asymptotic rate at which this process can be performed reliably. For several classes of quantum states, distillation above this rate obeys a strong converse: the fidelity with the target state vanishes asymptotically. Here we show that correlated catalysis removes the strong converse for every distillable bipartite state. Specifically, at any target rate $R>E_D$, the optimal asymptotic fidelity is given by $E_D/R$. Thus, although catalysis does not increase the maximum reliable distillation rate, it allows nonvanishing fidelity at every finite rate. Remarkably, this advantage persists even when the catalyst is returned exactly at every finite blocklength and the correlations between the output and catalyst vanish asymptotically. We further characterize the catalyst size required to sustain nonvanishing fidelity above the reliable distillation rate.
one_liner: Correlated catalysts let entanglement distillation above the reliable rate retain optimal asymptotic fidelity ED/R.
why_it_matters: Catalysis eliminates the strong converse without increasing the reliable distillation rate.

title: Universality and Emergent Classicality in Krylov Space
abstract: Krylov complexity grows linearly at late times for many systems. In this regime, we give a general spectral formula for the leading growth coefficients of Krylov complexity and its higher moments, without requiring detailed knowledge of the Lanczos coefficients. For states with a narrow energy distribution compared to the bandwidth, dynamics in the Krylov basis resembles motion along a classical trajectory. We demonstrate our results for the critical XY chain and double-scaled SYK. For the latter, we compute the leading late-time behavior of the chord-number moments through one-loop order.
one_liner: A spectral formula captures late-time growth of Krylov complexity moments and reveals effective classical motion for narrow-energy states.
why_it_matters: It provides universal late-time predictions without requiring detailed Lanczos coefficients.

title: Spin SYK-dot chains: entanglement bound and resource estimates towards a quantum advantage
abstract: Ground states of Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev (SYK)-type models are volume-law entangled, which makes them costly both for tensor networks and for quantum hardware simulations. Thus, it remains unclear where quantum hardware could outperform classical simulation of such models. In this work, we study a spin SYK-dot chain, in which q dense SYK dots of p qubits are joined by single ZZ bonds of strength K. The entanglement across any cut is then bounded by floor(p/2) ln 2 plus the inter-dot entanglement, and the two-qubit depth of one Trotter step is set by p alone. A resource estimate shows that a quantum advantage for the ground state could appear only for dots of about 15 to 21 qubits or more. There, a single Trotter step already requires two-qubit error rates of order 10^{-6}, beyond the reach of noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) hardware. We test the assumptions of this estimate with an imaginary-time matrix product state (MPS) that applies each dot as one block. It agrees with exact diagonalisation at (p, q) = (6, 2). At (5, 2), a variational circuit with the same dot-plus-link layout comes within 3.6% of the exact energy, and noisy simulations show that its fidelity decays as assumed in the resource estimate. At (8, 5), i.e., N = 40 qubits, the energy converges at bond dimension chi = 768, far below the exact value 2^20, and the inter-dot entanglement stays small and is set mainly by K. Out-of-time-order correlators across the links decay on a time scale that shrinks rapidly with |K|. Thus, the dot size p and the inter-dot coupling K together set the entanglement of the chain, and with it where a quantum advantage could appear.
one_liner: Resource estimates for spin SYK-dot chains place plausible quantum advantage at dot sizes of roughly 15–21 qubits or larger.
why_it_matters: The required two-qubit error rates near 10^-6 put this advantage beyond current NISQ hardware.

title: Dynamics of Fock states in traveling pulses
abstract: The quantum state of a traveling light pulse can qualitatively change the excitation dynamics of a two-level atom. We investigate this dependence for coherent and Fock input states using a virtual-cavity formulation with matched input and output temporal profiles. Analytical treatment of the master equation and numerical simulations show that coherent pulses produce damped Rabi oscillations, whereas Fock pulses can exhibit a partial recovery of the oscillation amplitude in the trailing part of the pulse. We examine how coupling to an auxiliary temporal mode and radiative loss shape this recovery. We also establish a connection with stimulated Raman adiabatic passage through an exact many-photon dark state and derive the associated adiabaticity condition. The observed recovery occurs away from ideal dark-state following. These results distinguish transient recovery in traveling-pulse scattering from conventional cavity collapse and revival, and clarify the scope of an adiabatic-transfer interpretation.
one_liner: Traveling Fock pulses can partially recover atomic Rabi-oscillation amplitude, unlike the damped response produced by coherent pulses.
why_it_matters: The work distinguishes transient pulse-scattering recovery from cavity revival and ideal adiabatic transfer.

title: Qyantram: A Transparent and Verifiable Quantum Computing Platform
abstract: Most quantum circuit platforms focus on idealized circuit assembly and simulation, hiding hardware compilation, error identification, and variational model training behind black-box operations. QYANTRAM addresses this gap through an open platform comprising four subsystems, built around evidence-backed results and independent verification. Its staged compilation pipeline makes every transformation traceable, while the router publishes rejected SWAP candidates and their scores for transparent decision-making. Verification exploits inactive qubits remaining in the |0> state, reducing complexity from 2^N to 2^k for k active qubits. This mathematically exact reduction enables full pre-compilation verification on 127- and 156-qubit layouts, achieving approximately 10,000x speed-ups with execution times below one millisecond. The error identification engine exhaustively evaluates all Pauli error patterns without sampling, matching closed-form predictions within 2.8e-17. Its machine-learning engine achieves numerical agreement within 2.0e-15 of qiskit.quantum_info while training 25-50 times faster. The router introduces approximately 1.27x more SWAP gates than Qiskit's SABRE due to its omission of optimization, trading routing efficiency for complete decision transparency and traceability.
one_liner: Qyantram exposes compilation, routing, verification, error analysis, and model training for independently auditable quantum workflows.
why_it_matters: It trades some routing efficiency for traceability while accelerating exact active-qubit verification.

title: Stabilizer Learning under Global Depolarizing Noise with Polynomial Copies and $2^t$ Time
